reason: I'll start with the loose cloud to see how the young stars make nearby gas shine.
expectation: I expect the stars' light to illuminate or energize the loose gas, though I'm unsure exactly how.

effect: The loose cloud is swept out of the nursery, opening a possible interaction with the hot bridge rather than clearly completing a shining-gas goal.
reaction: I was surprised that the loose gas was driven away rather than simply made to shine.
reason: I'll try the dense cloud to see how it responds differently to the young stars.
expectation: The dense gas may be illuminated or heated differently, though I don't know the exact result.

effect: The dense cloud leaves shielded pillars, completing the goal about what remains of the original cloud.
reaction: The contrast between the eroded surface and protected interior is satisfying.
reason: I'll try the thin cloud fringe with the young stars to pursue the remaining shining-gas goal.
expectation: I expect the stars to make the fringe glow, though the mechanism is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The outflow meeting the hot bridge is interesting, but the fringe seems more directly connected to the remaining goal.

effect: The thin fringe glows through hydrogen ionization and recombination, providing one apparent way to make gas shine.
reaction: The explanation of the glow was clear and satisfying.
reason: I'll try the nursery outflow against the hot bridge as a possible second way to make gas shine.
expectation: The colliding gases may produce luminous heated gas, though I am guessing.

alternatives.reason: The outflow could also affect the pillars, but the bridge seems a more plausible source of another glow.

effect: The outflow mixed with the bridge rather than producing the expected second glow, so I need to try another interaction.
reaction: It was interesting to see material from two different histories mix.
reason: I'll try the outflow against the dense pillars as another possible way to make gas shine.
expectation: The flow may shock and heat gas at the pillars' surfaces, but I'm unsure whether it will glow.

alternatives.reason: Infalling gas might also produce light, but the outflow and pillars seem a plausible interaction to test first.

effect: The outflow carries dense clumps away rather than producing the second glow, leaving the two infall combinations to explore.
reaction: The surviving dense interiors are interesting, though my glow prediction was wrong again.
reason: I'll try gas falling toward the growing stars; infall may release energy as light.
expectation: The falling gas may heat up and glow, though I'm unsure.

alternatives.reason: Dusty gas falling into the disk also fits the system, but the other infall seems more directly related to glowing gas.

effect: The infalling gas produced a narrow jet, opening an interaction with the hot bridge rather than immediately making gas glow.
reaction: I was surprised that some incoming matter is redirected outward.
reason: I'll combine the jet with the bridge; it's the only available action and may produce the second glow.
expectation: The jet may shock and heat the bridge gas, making it shine, though I'm unsure.

effect: The jet's impact produces shock-heated glowing gas, completing the second shining-gas goal and the chapter.
reaction: The contrast with the ionized fringe's glow was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the fringe glow was worthwhile because it clearly explained ionization and recombination.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying successive interactions for the second glow felt somewhat repetitive, especially when neither produced it.

surprise.text: I was surprised that some gas falling toward the young star is redirected outward in a jet.

arbitrary.text: The jet's eventual collision with the bridge was not an obvious route to the second glow beforehand, though the shock explanation made sense afterward.

continue.text: Yes, I'd continue: the different paths of the gas and their later interactions made me curious, despite some repetitive searching.
